correctness.rationale: The sharp <=3 proof follows invertible cyclic similarity and transpose invariance of products of symmetric exponentials; <=2 vertices give commuting adjacencies. Standard-library exact rational checker recomputes both four-phase matrices, characteristic polynomials, and strict Perron comparison vectors; all 24 four-factor orders are classified by two polynomials. The nonlinear SIS period maps are cooperative, positivity-improving and strictly subhomogeneous, proving global extinction for rho<1 and unique attracting endemic orbit for rho>1. Boundaries and finite stochastic limitations are explicitly restricted.

evidence: Sejunti et al. periodic SIS article gives Floquet criterion and examples with two alternating snapshots, including three-node weighted networks; Allen et al. address arbitrary snapshot order but transient changes. The own alternating-stars theorem fixes two balanced contact phases.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These frameworks entail ability to calculate a product but do not, without the new minimality argument and exact four-factor certificate, imply that the first possible order-dependent periodic SIS *threshold* needs four snapshots and three loopless undirected nodes.

evidence: Sejunti–Taylor–Masuda analyze epidemic-threshold reversals for a pair of static networks and say they use two phases; Allen–Moore–Hébert-Dufresne show chronology can change finite-time epidemic dynamics using graph commutators; Cai–Nie–Holme study stochastic activity-driven evolution; the own two-phase star example varies dwell duration.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The novel conclusion is not that noncommuting matrices affect dynamics or that two-phase SIS thresholds depend on dwell times. It is the universal invariance of periodic asymptotic Floquet growth under any reorder of <=3 undirected snapshots, together with a minimal four-phase, three-node binary *global outcome* switch for identical contact exposures and equal total period. A generic Floquet criterion alone does not supply the sharpness certificate.

evidence: Cyclic similarity and transpose reversal yield exact equality of Floquet spectra for up to three symmetric factors. Allen et al. provide time-ordered product and commutator expansion (arXiv:2205.11566v3, equations 2–6) but do not state sharp three-versus-four phase spectral permutation boundary.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Equivalent terminology examined: contact chronology/reordering, symmetric-matrix factor permutation, Floquet monodromy, epidemic threshold and time-respecting paths. Earlier work concerns transient state differences and error from aggregation, whereas this statement is invariant *asymptotic spectral growth* through three phases and strict threshold reversal at four.

originality.rationale: The three-snapshot invariance and sharp four-snapshot/three-vertex exact threshold reversal were compared by statement and implication with periodic SIS Floquet literature, chronology-compression work, and the accessible prior research ledger. A two-snapshot switching threshold or generic product formula does not state or certify this sharp minimal phase/vertex boundary. Priority risk remains for specialized matrix-product rearrangement literature.
residual_risks: A general symmetric-matrix product permutation theorem may express three-factor spectral invariance in another language; the specific sharp contact/epidemic consequence was not identified.
Full inspection of every relevant 2015 temporal SIS source was not available; the available abstracts and partial material are weaker evidence than a full read.
Search-index nonappearance and partition boundaries cannot establish global priority.

value.rationale: The threshold at which temporal chronology becomes relevant to periodic epidemic invasion is exactly four snapshots and three agents for undirected loopless contacts. Unlike routine numeric switching examples, the theorem establishes universal three-phase invariance and a sharp endpoint with exact rational strict stability certificates and opposite globally attracting nonlinear outcomes at a fixed aggregate contact budget. This directly addresses the biologically motivated distinction between exposure quantities and their timing.
